Islamic finance instruments

Murabaha

المرابحة

Also called: Murabahah; cost-plus sale

Definition

Murabaha is a Shariah-compliant sale in which the seller discloses what an asset cost and sells it at that cost plus an agreed profit, often with payment deferred.

What it means

In a Murabaha used for financing, a bank buys the asset a client needs and then sells it to the client at its cost plus a disclosed profit. The client pays the price in installments over an agreed period.

The profit is part of the sale price and is agreed at the outset; it is not interest on a loan. For the sale to be valid, the seller must own the asset, and carry the risk of owning it, before selling it on. Banks use Murabaha widely for asset and trade finance.

How HAYKALAH uses it

Murabaha is one of the Shariah contracts that FINA. and HAYKALAH’s work with banks draw on. In HAYKALAH’s method the contract follows from the asset and its cash flows, not the other way round, and the institution’s own Shariah board approves the structure.
